title: Keep His name free of anything small.
subtitle: The first word of the surah is a command to glorify
then: One of the earliest surahs of Makkah. The Prophet ﷺ recited it in the Eid and Friday prayers, and whenever he read this first line he would answer: {reward}Glory to my Lord, the Most High.{/reward} The surah opens with {idea}the right picture of Allah{/idea} before anything else.
now: You pray on autopilot. Or you quietly imagine Allah as tired of you, like a boss who has run out of patience. That picture shapes everything after it. {idea}Start by fixing the picture:{/idea} He is higher than your worst guess about Him.
old: I talk about Allah as if He thinks and tires like I do.
new: Every thought of Him should start above every flaw I know.
try: Next time you read this verse, pause and answer it out loud: Subhana rabbiyal a'la.

title: He made you, then He made you right.
subtitle: Creation, and then the fine tuning of every form
then: After the call to glorify, the surah gives the first reason. Allah {idea}created everything, then fashioned each creation in the best of forms.{/idea} Glory is not asked for in the air. It rests on what He has done.
now: The mirror in the morning. The filter on your phone camera. The thing about your body you wish you could swap. {idea}Every part of you was proportioned on purpose,{/idea} including the parts you complain about.
old: I look at myself and mostly see what is wrong.
new: I was shaped with care by the One I am told to glorify.
try: Thank Allah for one part of your body that works today without you thinking about it.

title: Everything got a measure and a direction.
subtitle: Allah decreed a measure and guided creation to it
then: Mujahid explained it: {idea}He guided people to the way of misery and of happiness, and guided cattle to their pastures.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to Musa's words to Pharaoh: our Lord gave each thing its form, then guided it.
now: A bird crosses a continent without a phone. A baby finds its mother's milk on day one. And you, at 2am, scrolling for answers about what to do with your life. {reward}You were also given a direction.{/reward} The question is whether you are listening for it.
old: I feel like I have to work out my whole life with no guidance.
new: The One who guides birds and cattle did not leave me without a path.
try: Before a decision today, ask Allah plainly for guidance in your own words.

title: The green came from Him, not from the soil.
subtitle: Allah brings out every kind of plant and crop

picture.label: What comes out of the ground

row.title: pasture
sub: all kinds of plants and crops

row.title: He brings it out
sub: every green thing is His act

then: The listeners in Makkah lived by pasture. Their camels and sheep ate what the land gave after rain. The verse points at that daily sight: {idea}it is Allah who brings out all types of vegetation and crops.{/idea}
now: The vegetables in the supermarket. The bread on your table. The coffee you drink before work. {idea}Every one started as something He brought out of the ground.{/idea} You rarely think past the shop shelf.
old: Food comes from the shop and the farmer.
new: Before the farmer and the shop, Allah brought it out of the earth.
try: At your next meal, name where one item on the plate grew before it reached you.

title: The green field turns to dark stubble.
subtitle: What grows bright also dries up and changes
then: Ibn Abbas said the stubble is {trap}dried up and altered.{/trap} The same hand that brings the pasture out also turns it brown. The listeners saw both every year. The surah later returns to this: {idea}this world does not last.{/idea}
now: Old photos of you at twenty. The car that was new. The job title that felt like everything. {trap}It all yellows.{/trap} Not as a tragedy, just as how this world works. {idea}What you build for the next life does not.{/idea}
old: If I hold on hard enough, the good season stays.
new: Every green season here is meant to turn. I plan for what does not.
try: Look at one old photo of yourself and say one thing you want to have done before the next one.

title: Do not worry, you will not forget it.
subtitle: A promise to the Prophet ﷺ about the revelation
then: This was revealed when the Prophet ﷺ was still not used to receiving revelation and {trap}feared he would forget its words.{/trap} Allah reassured him: {reward}We will make you recite, and you will not forget.{/reward}
now: You memorise a surah, then lose half of it after Ramadan. You read a page and nothing sticks. You start to feel this is not for you. {idea}The Quran is kept by the One who sent it.{/idea} Your part is to keep coming back.
old: If I cannot hold it all in my head, I have failed.
new: Allah promised to keep His words. I just need to keep showing up.
try: Recite one short surah you already know, slowly, without trying to learn anything new.

title: He knows what you say and what you hide.
subtitle: Except what Allah wills, and He sees both sides

row.title: Allah
sub: none of it hidden from Him

then: The promise of not forgetting has one exception: {idea}what Allah wills{/idea}, which He Himself removes, with no sin on the Prophet ﷺ for it. Then the reason: {idea}He knows what creatures do openly and what they hide.{/idea}
now: The version of you in the family group chat. The version on LinkedIn. The version alone with your phone at night. {idea}He knows all three.{/idea} That is not only a warning. It means the good you do in secret is seen too.
old: What nobody sees does not really count.
new: The hidden me is as known to Allah as the public me.
try: Do one small good thing today that no one will ever find out about.

title: We will ease you toward the easy way.
subtitle: Good deeds and a just, easy path made light
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}We will make good deeds and statements easy for you{/reward}, and give a law that is easy, tolerant, straight and just, with no crookedness or hardship. Said to a Prophet ﷺ carrying a mission alone in Makkah.
now: You picture being a better Muslim as a mountain: wake at 4am, read for hours, never slip. So you never start. {idea}The path was made easy on purpose.{/idea} Ask for ease, and take the first small step.
old: Being good has to feel hard, or it is not real.
new: Allah eases the way toward good for the one who turns to it.
try: Pick the smallest good habit you have been putting off and do it once today.

title: Remind people, where reminding helps.
subtitle: The etiquette of sharing what you know

row.title: remind where it benefits
sub: at their level, at the right time

then: After the promises, the task: {idea}remind, where reminding is beneficial.{/idea} Ibn Kathir draws the etiquette of spreading knowledge from it. Ali said: {trap}tell people what their minds can grasp{/trap}, or it becomes a trial for some of them.
now: The cousin you lecture at every family dinner. The forwarded message you post in a group that only starts a fight. {idea}The same truth, said at the wrong moment, closes doors.{/idea} Choose the time and the words.
old: If it is true, I should say it, however it lands.
new: A reminder is for helping. I share it where it can actually help.
try: Before your next piece of advice to someone, ask yourself whether now is the moment it can help.

title: The one who fears Allah will take the reminder.
subtitle: Who actually benefits when the truth is said
then: Ibn Kathir: the one {reward}whose heart fears Allah and knows he is going to meet Him{/reward} will take admonition from what the Prophet ﷺ conveys. The words are the same for all. {idea}The listener's heart decides what they do.{/idea}
now: A Friday khutbah. Two people sit side by side. One leaves changed, the other checks the football score on the way out. {idea}The difference is not the speaker.{/idea} It is what each brought into the room.
old: Reminders do not work on me, they are boring.
new: A reminder works when my heart remembers I will meet Allah.
try: Before the next talk or reading you hear, remind yourself for ten seconds that you will meet Allah.
